properties.foundation_analysis:
- **Subterranean Bedrock & Subsurface Dynamics:** The site occupies alluvial terrace deposits of the Atlantic Coastal Plain overlying crystalline metamorphic bedrock (gneiss/schist) of the Piedmont Fall Zone. The foundation rests on massive stepped bluestone gneiss masonry reinforced with concrete sub-footings to stabilize the weight above high Potomac River alluvial water tables.
- **Indigenous Masonry Lithics:**
  - *Washington Monument:* Three distinct lithic strata across its vertical rise. The lower ~152 feet (1848–1854) is faced with coarse-grained calcitic marble quarried from Texas, Baltimore County, Maryland. Above a distinct horizontal shift line, four transitional courses consist of fine Stockbridge dolomitic marble from Sheffield/Lee, Massachusetts. The upper two-thirds (1879–1884 completion) is faced with fine-grained dolomitic Cockeysville marble (Beaver Dam Quarry, Maryland), backed by Maine granite and Seneca red sandstone.
  - *Federal Triangle & Background Civic Buildings:* Clad extensively in Salem Formation Indiana oolitic limestone, with lower rusticated basements set in gray crystalline granite.
- **Mortar Chemistry:** Traditional non-hydraulic to semi-hydraulic high-calcium lime mortar in the historic masonry seams, with repointed elastomeric and natural cementitious formulations at high-exposure joints.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis:
- **Vegetative Canvas & Canopy Structure:**
  - The Monument Grounds and Mall are blanketed in dense, manicured Kentucky bluegrass and tall fescue turfgrass, traced by packed decomposed granite/gravel pedestrian pathways.
  - Surrounding mature tree clusters disambiguated from built forms: American Elm (*Ulmus americana*), Pin Oak (*Quercus palustris*), Willow Oak (*Quercus phellos*), London Plane (*Platanus occidentalis x acerifolia*), and Yoshino Cherry (*Prunus x yedoensis*), displaying dense, multi-tonal green organic leaf foliage and natural branch architecture.

properties.architectural_summary:
- **Typologies & Massing:**
  - *Center Obelisk:* Free-standing stone masonry Egyptian Revival/Classical obelisk rising to an exact height of 554 ft 7+11⁄32 in (169.05 m), tapering to an acute 55-foot pyramidion capped with an aluminum apex.
  - *Center-Right Middleground (NMAAHC):* National Museum of African American History and Culture featuring a three-tiered inverted ziggurat/corona structure wrapped in bronze-colored cast-aluminum latticework.
  - *Background Civic Core (Federal Triangle / Constitution Ave):* Neoclassical and Beaux-Arts monumental office blocks (Herbert C. Hoover / Department of Commerce, Ronald Reagan Building, EPA/Clinton Building) characterized by colossal multi-column colonnades, pedimented porticos, denticulated friezes, and low-pitch red-orange Spanish terra-cotta tile hip roofs.
- **Planar Rectification & Geometric Orthogonality:** Absolute true vertical alignment applied to the 555-foot obelisk shaft. Middleground and background facades rectified to plumb 90-degree lines; terra-cotta roof ridgelines and horizontal cornices aligned across the entire urban horizon.
